findings: certs/fei-ledger.json prints the ratio's two ends as the same 44-character string 6.521845710923046575658143972948578468366662: both are truncations (str(...)[:44] in fei.py), so the printed upper end is BELOW the value (the ratio begins 6.521845710923046575658143972948578468366662292229…). Read honestly the enclosure is [6.521845710923046575658143972948578468366662, 6.521845710923046575658143972948578468366663]; its H strings are truncated the same way. Nothing is wrong with the decision — fei.py decides on the untruncated Decimals — only with the record's printed interval.

fei.py has two words (CERTIFIED when every check passes, REFUTED otherwise): on 6 of the 12 planted claims its own word is REFUTED where the three-word reading is REFUSED (b-one-bit-flipped, c-unbalanced-binding-bypassed, e1-stated-influence-moved, e2-bar-1e-75-below-the-value, e3-bar-1e-75-above-the-value, e6-majority-of-three-at-4) — a broken binding, an unbalanced table, a contradicted I and a bar inside its enclosure are all printed REFUTED, the defect the 2026-10-09 erratum removed from families/cosine.js and families/newman.js. On e2-bar-1e-75-below-the-value, a TRUE claim, fei.py's own word is REFUTED. No published record is affected: the ledger's one row is CERTIFIED, which two words get right.

At an exact boundary (majority of three, H/(I-1) = 4 exactly, against "> 4") the closed form refutes and fei.py cannot: every log2 it takes is an interval one unit wide, log2 4 included. A refusal a stronger method converts.

On the dictator fei.py refuses by raising "ArithmeticError: a weight above 1" — the weight is exactly 1, but its log2 enclosure of 2^n is wider than a point, so 2n - 2 log2 |a| has a negative lower end and it raises before reaching its I <= 1 test. instruments/fei/battery.py's red control "a dictator (I = 1) is refused: the amplification rule needs I > 1" therefore fires for that other reason (it catches any ArithmeticError).
